note: Research snapshot of pending Australian AML/CTF developments affecting legal practices. Every item is a watch item, not an obligation. Confirm each against its primary source at use time.

watch_items.item: Ministerial guidelines on legal professional privilege claims under section 242A
watch_items.status_at_snapshot: AUSTRAC's LPP guidance (last updated 1 July 2026) states the Minister for Home Affairs will issue guidelines covering review and challenge of LPP claims, further-information requests, handling of privileged information in searches and dispute resolution; not released at snapshot
watch_items.expected_trigger: Making of the final guidelines by the Minister as a notifiable instrument under section 242A
watch_items.status_at_review: Draft consulted, final not made on the public record. The Department of Home Affairs page for the Draft Legal Professional Privilege Guidelines 2026 (last updated 8 July 2026) says the Department and AUSTRAC are progressing work to finalise the Guidelines; a first targeted round closed 1 August 2025 and the consultation on the current draft closed 24 June 2026. On 16 Nov 2026 a Federal Register of Legislation search returned no s 242A instrument, and AUSTRAC's LPP guidance page (last updated 1 July 2026) still says the Minister 'will issue' guidelines. The Home Affairs page states that s 242A commences on 1 July 2026
watch_items.review_basis: homeaffairs.gov.au page read on 2026-11-16 from a copy the maintainer downloaded (the site blocks automated access); Federal Register search and austrac.gov.au page read on 2026-11-16

watch_items.item: Amendments to the Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Terrorism Financing Rules 2025 and transitional rules
watch_items.status_at_snapshot: The AML/CTF Rules 2025 (F2025L01026) commenced 31 March 2026 (latest compilation F2026C00274). The AML/CTF Transitional Rules 2026 (F2026L00393) set staged deadlines: compliance-officer notification for newly regulated entities by the later of 14 days after enrolment or 29 July 2026; first independent evaluation of the program by 30 June 2029 to 31 December 2030 depending on the last two digits of the AUSTRAC account number; IFTI-to-IVTS reporting transition on 31 March 2029. Further amendment instruments are expected as the reform settles
watch_items.expected_trigger: Registration of amendment or transitional instruments on the Federal Register of Legislation
watch_items.status_at_review: The latest compilation of the AML/CTF Rules 2025 is still F2026C00274 (31 March 2026). The Transitional Rules 2026 (F2026L00393) now have a compilation, F2026C00452 (14 May 2026), incorporating the AML/CTF Transitional Amendment (Reporting Obligations) Rules 2026 (F2026L00556), which commenced 14 May 2026, changes s 10(5) to refer to Division 3A of Part 9 of the AML/CTF Rules 2025 and adds an application provision (s 21). Nothing in this plugin cites s 10(5). The 29 July 2026 fixed date for compliance-officer notification by newly regulated entities has passed; for entities enrolling later, only the 14-days-after-enrolment limb operates
watch_items.review_basis: legislation.gov.au version lists and the text of F2026L00556 read on 2026-11-16

watch_items.item: First annual compliance report cycle for tranche 2 reporting entities
watch_items.status_at_snapshot: AUSTRAC's obligations summary describes an annual compliance report about how obligations were met the previous calendar year; the first cycle covering tranche 2 entities' 2026 obligations, and its lodgement window, had not been the subject of dedicated tranche 2 guidance located at snapshot
watch_items.expected_trigger: AUSTRAC Online opening of the first financial-year compliance-report window, or any AUSTRAC notice changing the reporting period
watch_items.status_at_review: No change. AUSTRAC's annual compliance reports page still gives the next reporting period as 1 July 2026 to 30 June 2027, with reports due within 3 months of the period ending (a 1 July to 30 September submission window). On that basis (an inference; the page does not address tranche 2 specifically) the first tranche 2 report would cover 1 July 2026 to 30 June 2027 and be due by 30 September 2027
watch_items.review_basis: austrac.gov.au annual compliance reports page read on 2026-11-16

watch_items.item: Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Terrorism Financing Amendment Bill 2026
watch_items.status_at_snapshot: Not on the register at the 14 August 2026 snapshot
watch_items.expected_trigger: Passage by both Houses, Royal Assent and commencement, followed by any AUSTRAC guidance on the changed LPP-form process
watch_items.status_at_review: Passed both Houses, not yet law. Introduced 12 Mar 2026; House third reading 16 Sep 2026 with 25 Government amendments; Senate second and third readings agreed to on 16 Nov 2026 with no Senate amendment recorded; the Parliament page shows 'Passed Both Houses' and no Royal Assent, and no Act is registered on legislation.gov.au. (Act No. 86, 2026, shown in the 1 Oct 2026 AML/CTF Act compilation, is a different Act.) As passed, Schedule 1 commences 1 July 2027, Schedule 2 on the 28th day after assent, and Schedule 3 Part 3 at the later of immediately after Schedule 4 to the 2024 amending Act commences and the day after assent. Schedule 3 Part 3 items 14 to 16 (s 49) and 20 to 22 (s 202) require the recipient of a notice to give the LPP form to the issuer of the notice, items 17 to 19 add s 176(1A) so that the issuer or the AUSTRAC CEO may apply for a civil penalty order, and item 23 applies the changes to notices given on or after commencement. Until assent and commencement the current law is unchanged
watch_items.review_basis: aph.gov.au bill page and the ParlInfo as-passed text of Schedule 3 Part 3 read on 2026-11-16; legislation.gov.au checked for a registered Act on the same day
